# Moving regular Morison source force

The five eight-state CSVs are direct evaluations of WEC-Sim core commit
`0753b2e47f2457c078751dcfe5d251d1767b80ab` with MATLAB R2025b.
`reference_model_baseline.m` generated the option-1 state/force CSV in the
earlier source run. `tests/matlab/morison_moving_force_probe.m` reads its saved
states, rechecks option 1 against the pinned source function, then generates
the other four CSVs without rerunning the 400 s Simulink model.
The pinned `regWaveMorison.m` SHA-256 is
`b8a11b4d2814dc3baae3b27f3b64713768890ef4e1bb358413a11cd7f4c0ad38`.
Each row contains time, six body position components, six velocities, six
accelerations, and six source force and moment components. The filenames below
share the `MORISON_MOVING_` prefix.

| CSV suffix | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `REGULAR_states.csv` | `466ff5a912ca07062d699f9275e6ea2db2ae42b20ee3b6844a967e53f96ca827` |
| `NORMAL_TANGENTIAL_states.csv` | `ce0014df5dea6638b747b33c42166bfca6563c86e5fdc3c970de8f8221e0d81e` |
| `REGULAR_CURRENT_uniform_states.csv` | `a9bc61ea3822c9f39c7c97e5e08ebf4de3bb7c5abaec54dffc641f6f4328c48f` |
| `REGULAR_CURRENT_power_states.csv` | `3c69e1d2cdcf6effa396e5f0dc3938fc36c9749e5c769bb3b78ddc53ff0b30b2` |
| `REGULAR_CURRENT_linear_states.csv` | `8e9e01f85122e13c86c8176356d75aa8ac19feb7efaa382bace253b6fca3acff` |

The freshly re-evaluated regular option-1 force agrees within `1e-9` in its
units with the archived source values. That archived CSV is byte-identical to the earlier
[R2025b run 37768083149](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/37768083149)
after a separate regeneration on mali. The four archived outputs were also
regenerated byte-identically by the focused probe on mali.

The portable tests evaluate Python's source-law diagnostics at all eight saved
states, including a wave ramp, nonzero rotation, an emerged element, the
normal/tangential option, and three current profiles.
These prescribed states do not establish coupled moving-body parity. The
separate physical axial-law test protects its rigid rotation and dissipative
relative-velocity behavior; [WEC-Sim issue #1664](https://github.com/WEC-Sim/WEC-Sim/issues/1664)
tracks the nonorthogonal matrix retained only by the Python source diagnostic.
